messages.subject: how to prevent mplusModeler() run all mplus input files in the same directory?
messages.subject_clean: how to prevent mplusModeler() run all mplus input files in the same directory?
messages.body_plain:
Usually I run several SEM models one by one using `mplusModeler()`, and I'd like to put all mplus syntax files into one foler. How ever, I see that `mplusModeler()` will run all the input files within the directory. Is there any way to tell mplusModeler() to run jun the syntax file indicated by its `object` argument? Perhaps setting the `filefilter` argument of `runModels` will do the trick?

Any thoughts to fix this?

messages.body_plain:
The LL difference is in the summaries, but was inadvertently left out of the documentation. If you look within the $summaries object for a model extracted by readModels, you should see

BLRT_2xLLDiff: 2x ll diff
BLRT_ParamDiff: difference in number of parameters for k and k-1 models.

Other info about the BLRT is also in the object, which you can see with str(modelObj$summaries)

I'll add these differences to the documentation.

Michael

messages.subject: Re: Multiple group analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tait,

Because parameter estimates vary so much in their contents, we haven't developed a function for presenting these. But I would encourage you to look at the xtable package (e.g., http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/xtable/vignettes/xtableGallery.pdf), which is very capable of making custom tables in LaTeX and HTML. HTML can often be pasted directly into MS programs like Excel, whereas the LaTeX can be formatted easily into PDFs using tools like TexShop.

library(xtable)
m <- readModels("myModel.out")
print(xtable(m$unstandardized), type="html")

Hope that helps,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: Save additional estimates in output (from a mediation model)
messages.subject_clean: Save additional estimates in output (from a mediation model)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Cathy,

I'm a user of the MplusAutomation package and have been able to obtain mediation estimates when reading the Mplus output file into R.  Rather than using the MODEL INDIRECT command in Mplus you can manually define all mediation effects of interest by labeling the relevant path estimates and then calculating the mediated effect in MODEL CONSTRAINT.  All new parameters defined in MODEL CONSTRAINT (e.g., your specific mediated effects) are read in with other parameter estimates using the extractModelParameters function (which is also a part of the ReadModels function) in the MplusAutomation package.  Here is a brief example of how you would specify your mediation model in Mplus so that you can extract the mediated effect using the MplusAutomation in R:

MODEL:
  m ON x (p1) ; ! mediation a path (parameter is labeled p1)
  y ON x m (p2-p3) ; ! mediation c' and b paths (labeled p2 and p3, respectively)
MODEL CONSTRAINT:
  NEW (ab) ; ! create a new variable called 'ab'
  ab = p1 * p3 ; ! 'ab' mediated effect = a path * b path

I hope this helps everyone!
Amanda

messages.subject: readModels Error: More than one match found for parameter: ^\s*Number of observations\s*
messages.subject_clean: readModels Error: More than one match found for parameter: ^\s*Number of observations\s*
messages.body_plain:
Dear Michael,

I have found your MplusAutomation package to be extraordinarily useful and I cannot thank you enough for creating and maintaining this R package.  I have stumbled across an issue that I want to bring to your attention and would like to ask your advice on how to handle.  When reading in several Mplus output files in a directory using the readModels function I get the following error:

Error in extractValue(pattern = "^\\s*Number of observations\\s*", analysisSummarySection,  :
  More than one match found for parameter: ^\s*Number of observations\s*
  C:/MOTG Simulation - No Mediation - Test18/c13133/motg_xony_nom_c13133_r2.out

When I examine this particular Mplus output file it is evident what the problem is - data sparseness prevents the missing data EM algorithm from converging and this produces a message that includes the text "NUMBER OF OBSERVATIONS".  This is why the string search for "Number of observations" in the readModels function finds more than one match.  Here is the full message at the end of the COVARIANCE COVERAGE OF DATA section of the Mplus output file (immediately preceding "THE MODEL ESTIMATION TERMINATED NORMALLY"):

     THE MISSING DATA EM ALGORITHM FOR THE H1 MODEL
     HAS NOT CONVERGED WITH RESPECT TO THE PARAMETER
     ESTIMATES.  THIS MAY BE DUE TO SPARSE DATA
     LEADING TO A SINGULAR COVARIANCE MATRIX ESTIMATE.
     INCREASE THE NUMBER OF H1 ITERATIONS.

     NOTE THAT THE NUMBER OF H1 PARAMETERS (MEANS, VARIANCES, AND
     COVARIANCES) IS GREATER THAN THE NUMBER OF OBSERVATIONS.
               NUMBER OF H1 PARAMETERS :        135
               NUMBER OF OBSERVATIONS  :        131

I understand why the readModels function is crashing here but am unsure of how to handle this situation so that I can flag the problematic output file and/or move on to the next output file.  This issue came up in a small test run of a large simulation study.  I anticipate that this will happen numerous times in the full run of the simulation study and I need to figure out a way to read in all the Mplus output files without the readModels function crashing.  Any insight you could provide would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks much,
Amanda
